extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and principal investigators (PIs), including early-stage investigators
extracted.subtask_short: NIH grant funding and award process guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical Q&A guidance on NIH review, paylines, ESI/NI rules, JIT and administrative processes, Council review, supplements/competitive revisions, and interactions with Program Officers and Grants Management Specialists for applicants preparing, submitting, or awaiting NIH awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESI status: determination and effect on funding
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI status is determined at the time of submission and carries through review; however, the trans-IC policy (NOT-OD-19-072) means an ESI award will cancel ESI status for all other pending applications for that investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check current NIH policy and ask a PO about specific situations. Because of this policy change, award date (not submission date) is considered for maintaining ESI status across pending applications; the MIRA PO should be consulted before submitting an R01 if concerned about losing ESI-based consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Investigator (NI) and ESI definitions and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI must be a New Investigator (NI) and within 10 years of their terminal degree or the end of postgraduate training; medical residency counts as postgraduate training but non-clinical postdoc years do not count as postgraduate training for the 10-year clock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some ICs treat NI/ESI differently (definitions are NIH-wide, but recognition can be IC-specific). For MPI applications, all PIs on the MPI must be ESI to receive ESI special consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting impact scores and percentiles vs institute paylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact scores and percentiles have IC-specific funding implications; ICs publish or informally have paylines but bounds vary (examples: some think NINDS lower end around 10, many ICs may fund into the 20s; NIDA may be tighter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain your summary statement and contact your PO for advice on likelihood of funding and next steps (rebuttal, resubmission strategy). Do not infer final funding solely from community anecdotes—ask your PO for institute-specific context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact Program Officer (PO) after summary statement
rubrics_metrics.description: You should contact your PO after you receive the summary statement for advice on next steps, such as rebuttal, resubmission, or strategy for responding to reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs can advise on funding likelihood and strategy; if PO is unresponsive, consider copying the PO’s branch chief or checking for another appropriate PO in the IC portfolio (e.g., via RePORTER Matchmaker).

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles of PO vs Grants Management Specialist (GMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Officers advise on scientific/review matters and strategy; Grants Management Specialists handle award processing and administrative status (e.g., JIT handling, administrative holds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If status is ‘Pending administrative review’, the GMS is the primary contact for award processing status. Do not over-contact POs about administrative processing—they often cannot provide timing details while GMS is handling the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Pending administrative review' eRA status
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Pending administrative review’ indicates the application is in GMS/award processing and is often a positive signal (could mean award likely) but can remain for weeks to months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs may have no further information while administrative review is ongoing. Start date on the application is not an expiration date; you can prepare regulatory approvals before JIT, and you may send JIT materials early (they will just sit until needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT (Just-in-Time) requests and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: JIT requests are often automated; you may receive a JIT before speaking with a PO, and you can also submit JIT documents proactively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If regulatory approvals (IRB, IACUC, etc.) are required, start preparing them before JIT arrives. Submitting JIT materials earlier does not speed processing but prevents delays once award decisions progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council review and eRA Commons messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA Commons often shows 'Pending Council review' for many non-fellowship applications until Council meets; being on the list sent to Council is required for award consideration, but being on the list does not guarantee funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all applications are discussed by Council; Council approval is a step that makes applications eligible for award pending funding availability and IC Director decisions. Timing shown in eRA is approximate and varies by IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which applications are discussed vs triaged (Not Discussed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study sections typically triage roughly 40%-50% of applications; 'Not Discussed' means the application was not in the top half to be discussed, even if average reviewer scores seem decent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are ranked by preliminary scores and a threshold applied; any reviewer can request a triaged application be discussed, but many triaged apps receive no such advocates. Ask your PO for context about a particular study section's behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triage scoring interpretation and reviewer variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if your mean reviewer score seems good, relative rankings and distribution of other applications determine whether yours is discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the summary statement with your PO to understand panel dynamics and possible paths forward; resubmission strategies should not wait for eRA status changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission and new submission options after A0/A1
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have already submitted A0 and A1 (used the resubmission slot), you can submit a new A0 (a fresh application with a new grant number) rather than a resubmission, and you need not respond to prior review in the new A0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss timing and strategy with your PO. Do not rely on eRA Commons status as the trigger for resubmission—prepare in advance of the next submission cycle if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive Revisions vs NOSI vs Administrative Supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of Special Interest (NOSIs) and competitive revision announcements differ: some NOSIs encourage competitive revisions to active grants (requiring an active grant), while others ask applicants to submit new applications to parent FOAs and cite the Notice for special consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the specific Notice and parent FOA carefully and ask the PO which mechanism is intended (competitive revision vs new application citing NOSI). For COVID-related NOSIs, many ICs used parent FOAs with citation of the Notice to get better payline consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and format for COVID-19 administrative supplements/competitive revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative supplements/competitive revisions typically require a Research Strategy that ties proposed work into the parent award and is often expected to be ~6 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your PO before preparing the supplement—POs discuss these internally and can advise whether your idea fits and how to frame it for program staff review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Support and 'current budget period' guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For JIT and Other Support calculations, 'current budget period' refers to the first budget year of the pending award; person-month calculations should reflect the level of effort in that current budget period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional sponsored programs or fiscal administrators can advise on including startup funds, amounts remaining, and how to list NCEs; consult them for precise formatting and calculation examples (e.g., 0.25 effort over 3 months = 0.75 person-months).

rubrics_metrics.name: No-Cost Extension (NCE) and requesting additional time or funds
rubrics_metrics.description: You may request a second NCE if you still have unobligated funds, but you cannot request additional funds (no extra dollars) through an NCE from NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in need of bridge funding, check with your department or institution for internal support options (institutions sometimes provide bridge funds until you can renew or resubmit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with unresponsive POs
rubrics_metrics.description: PO responsiveness varies; if urgent and the PO is not replying, consider contacting another PO in the branch/division or copying the PO’s branch chief/division head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about escalation to avoid alienating an otherwise supportive PO; identify other staff via IC website or RePORTER Matchmaker if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of COVID-19 on timelines, paylines, and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: COVID-19 has caused delays in administrative processing (JIT/NoAs), but awards are not broadly being canceled; NIH issued some deadline extensions and COVID-specific FAQs indicating research shutdowns can be grounds for ESI extensions in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor NIH FAQs and Notices for updated policies (e.g., ESI extensions), and discuss specific concerns with your PO. Be prepared for slower processing but also potential new funding opportunities via admin supplements or NOSIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap and simultaneous awards (MIRA vs R01) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When two possible awards overlap (e.g., an ESI R01 and an ESI MIRA), you will typically receive one award; IC preferences and timing matter (some ICs prefer awarding MIRA over ESI R01s), and receiving one award can eliminate eligibility for the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss overlap and sequencing with the relevant POs before submission to understand how decisions and timing could affect eligibility and acceptance choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing expectations after Council and for NOA issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: After Council meets, final funding decisions and issuance of NoA can still take weeks to months; you might not hear immediate confirmation even after favorable Council actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be patient; maintain communication with your PO and GMS as appropriate, and prepare any regulatory approvals or institutional paperwork in advance to avoid delays once an award is processed.
